Roasting with intention since 2011

Meridian began as a one-kilo sample roaster in a Southeast Portland garage. Fifteen years later we still roast every batch on the same street, with the same obsession for the people who grow the coffee.

Our story

Founder Sofia Marchetti spent four seasons working harvests in Huila, Colombia before coming home to Portland with a notebook full of producer contacts and a stubborn belief that a roaster's first job is transparency. Meridian's first wholesale account was a food cart two blocks from our current café. We printed the farm, altitude, and price paid on every bag from day one — a practice that was unusual in 2011 and remains the core of how we operate.

Today we buy from fourteen producer partners across Colombia, Ethiopia, Kenya, and Guatemala, and we publish the price paid at farmgate for every lot on our transparency reports. Our sourcing philosophy is simple: long-term relationships, prices above the Fair Trade minimum, and pre-harvest financing for partners who want it.

What we stand for

Transparency

Every bag lists the farm, variety, altitude, and the price we paid at farmgate. Our 2026 transparency report is open to everyone.

Relationships

Our longest partnership is entering its twelfth harvest. We visit producing partners at least once a year and pay for samples — nobody works for us for exposure.

Community

We donate one cent per pound sold to the Portland Coffee Emergency Fund and host free public cuppings every Saturday at 10am.

Get in touch

Questions about wholesale, tours, or anything else? Send us a note — we answer everything within two business days.
